title: Talk it up or play it down? (Un)expected correlations between (de-)emphasis and recurrence of discussion points in consequential U.S. economic policy meetings
reasoning: The paper focuses on computational linguistics and rhetorical analysis within the context of economic policy meetings. It examines how language choices like hedging and superlatives correlate with idea uptake, specifically looking at social variables like gender and status. It contains no evaluation of religion, morals, or ethics.
